holidays.name: International Literacy Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the magic of reading and to remind everyone that being able to read a cereal box, a treasure map, or a bizarre holiday list is a superpower worth protecting.
holidays.origin: Proclaimed by UNESCO in 1965 and first celebrated in 1966 to highlight the importance of literacy as a matter of dignity and human rights.
holidays.funFact: The first International Literacy Day was celebrated in 1967, and UNESCO awards literacy prizes each year in connection with the observance.

holidays.name: Pardon Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to forgiveness, second chances, and wiping the slate clean, especially for political figures who might have gotten into a bit of a pickle.
holidays.origin: It marks the anniversary of September 8, 1974, when President Gerald Ford granted a full pardon to Richard Nixon for any crimes he may have committed while in office.
holidays.funFact: Ford's pardon came just one month after Nixon resigned, and it was so controversial that many historians believe it hurt Ford in the 1976 election.

holidays.name: Star Trek Day
holidays.description: Trekkies and casual sci-fi fans alike boldly go into celebration mode, binge-watching episodes, quoting Spock, and perhaps dressing in red shirts (at their own risk).
holidays.origin: Star Trek premiered on NBC on September 8, 1966, and the date has been celebrated by fans and the franchise ever since, with official recognition from Paramount in recent years.
holidays.funFact: The original series was canceled after three seasons, yet it grew into a multi-billion-dollar franchise with numerous spin-offs and movies.

holidays.name: National Date Nut Bread Day
holidays.description: A day to enjoy a slice of sweet, dense, nutty bread, ideally slathered with cream cheese or butter, and to ponder why dates and nuts have such a loyal following.
holidays.origin: Date nut bread became a popular American treat in the early 20th century, and this unofficial food holiday emerged to honor the humble loaf.
holidays.funFact: A classic date nut bread sandwich with cream cheese was once a famous lunch-counter staple at Woolworth's in the mid-20th century.

holidays.name: Ocean's Day... of Sailors? Not Quite: International Day of Sports for Dry-Land Fishermen? No: National Ampersand Day
holidays.description: A celebration of the humble & symbol, a typographic character that is a bit of a rebel, showing up in company names, wedding invitations, and your fanciest fonts.
holidays.origin: An unofficial observance created by typography fans to honor the ampersand, which dates back to ancient Rome, where scribes merged the letters E and T of the Latin word 'et'.
holidays.funFact: The ampersand was once the 27th letter of the English alphabet, and the name comes from schoolchildren reciting 'and per se and.'
